newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - June 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - June 16.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

The new management at Optus Communications intends to re-establish the firm as a specialist telecommunications carrier with an immediate restructuring and the eventual sale of its loss-making pay TV operations. This strategic move relects the fears of core shareholders that the pay TV business will continue to drag on profits. Page 1.

Low inflation has caused difficulty for companies and unions, with BHP forced to reduce its goals for return rates. BHP chief executive John Prescott has urged the industry not to view this move as failure, saying the company has not stopped aiming for the best, but has simply been forced to rethink what 'best' is. Page 1.

The Australian Olympic Committee expects to lose up to 80 per cent of its original A$7.2 million investment in the Reef Casino Trust, and is set to start negotiations to extract itself from the business. AOC chairman John Coats is disappointed that Reef' casino operator, Casinos Austria International Ltd, will come out of the deal better off, despite failing to perform. Page 23.

Development Australia Fund has scored a coup by gaining a stake in each of the three winning consortiums in the first-round of the airport privatisation biddings. DAF, which comprises of six industry superannuation funds and AMP Investments, has committed A$81.5 million to Melbourne, Brisbane and Perth airports. Page 23.

The most likely identity of the mystery buyer of a 14.74 per cent stake in troubled food giant Burns, Philp & Co Ltd is New Zealand entrepreneur Graeme Hart. While other contenders include US businessmen Klaus Friesner and Michael Spencer, Hart is the mot favoured due to his reputation for swooping on troubled stocks, using them as leverage in event of a takeover. Page 24.

The Myer family appears to have taken advantage of a rise in the share price of Coles Myer. A shareholder notice lodged with the Australian Stock Exchange by company director Martin Myer revealed that 9.8 million shares had been offloaded. Since November 19, the Coles Myer share price has surged from A$4.70 to last Friday's A$6.54. Page 27.
THE AUSTRALIAN

American energy group PacifiCorp, whose first overseas purchase was Victorian electricity distributor Powercor, has increased its presence in Australia with the US$9.6 billion agreed takeover of British-based The Energy Group. The Energy Group's subsidiay Peabody has more than 260 million tonnes of coal reserves in Australia. Page 17.

BancTec Australia, an imaging and cheque processing company, has won a A$66 million contract with Korean-based ChungHo computers to develop software that will capture images and data from a giro for the Korean Financial and Telecommunications Clearing Insitute. Page 17.

BHP and Westcoast Energy are still waiting on a decision by the Independent Pricing and Regulatory Tribunal which will confirm the viability of the proposed A$380 million Eastern Gas Pipeline, which would bring Bass Strait gas to major industry in New Souh Wales. Page 17.

A decision by Federal Small Business and Consumer Affairs Minister Geoff Prosser to cut funding to the Franchise Code Administration Council, which administers the self-regulatory code of practice established for franchises in 1993, has led to a debate over how the franchise sector should be regulated, and how franchisees can be protected. Page 17.

Both Boral and AGL have indicated they are keen to bid for the New South Wales Government's upcoming A$22 billion power industry sell-off, but they have warned investors they are not prepared to pay exorbitant prices to achieve their common goal of develoing comprehensive energy businesses. Page 19.

The latest Colonial State Bank survey of manufacturing in New South Wales has predicted the State's manufacturing industry will lose more than 2500 jobs in the next year amid an atmosphere of weakening profitability and low production. Page 19.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

In the lead up to the deregulation of the national gas market, Boral will today outline plans for its A$400 million sharemarket listing of Envestra Ltd, a subsidiary which handles a slice of Boral's A$1.5 billion energy assets. Envestra will own and operte gas distribution businesses in Queensland, South Australia, and the Northern Territory, and will service over 400,000 customers. Page 37.

The latest change in Australia's superannuation industry - giving employees a choice in superannuation funds - is a move seen by the Federal Government as a way of loosening the stranglehold on employee super by union-backed funds. The change will see coporate and industry super funds competing for membership with retail fund managers and life insurance companies. Page 37.

Stockbrokers will have to lodge their final bids for Imperial Chemical Industries plc's A$2.2 billion shareholding of its Australian arm by next Monday. Shares in ICI will be made available to existing shareholders, retail investors and institutions. Pag 37.

A spokesman for Energy Resources Australia says a final environmental impact study into the development of the controversial Jabiluka uranium deposit in the Northern Territory will be released tomorrow. While ERA says the report addresses all issues raisd in response to a draft statement in October, there continues to be strong opposition from environmentalists and traditional landowners. Page 37.

Lend Lease Corp managing director David Higgins has announced the property and financial services group is comfortable with its business mix and has no immediate plans for any major asset sales. The company is well on the track to achieve its three-year oal of reducing costs to 40 per cent. Page 39.

The Federal Government yesterday set an August deadline for legislation on the sale of debt-laden rail operator Australian National. Federal Transport Minister John Sharp said more than 50 concerns had expressed interest in buying AN, but the bidding proess has already been delayed by strong opposition from the Democrats and Labor. Page 39.
THE AGE The sale of Imperial Chemical Industries plc's A$2.2 billion shareholding in its Australian subsidiary draws nearer with next Monday's deadline for submitting final bid documents.
ICI announced the sale of a 62.4 per cent stake in its Australian arm on May 7, in a move intended to help fund the A$10 billion purchase of Unilever's chemical divisions. Page B1 --

Australian share prices are expected to reach new highs with traders more confident of another interest rate cut, coupled with a strong Wall Street performance last Friday night. A Reuters survey of 30 Australian market economists revealed expectations o a 59 per cent chance of a rate cut. Page B1.

Normandy Mining and its Canadian partner have resumed the development of the Ovacik mine in Turkey following a month-long halt in construction work due to demonstrations by environmentalists. The A$61 million high-grade underground and open-cut operatio is scheduled for commissioning at the end of the year. Page B2.

Investors looking for exposure to nickle in the local market have a range of advanced development and exploration projects to choose from. While WMC and QNI are still the only ones producing nickle, there are many new wave projects producing lateritic ores in Western Australia. Page B3.

Hallmark Gold NL has made a 15 cents-a-share capital return to shareholders and plans to become more active and aggressive, reflecting its status as a well-funded junior explorer. The company plans to have an annual exploration spend of between A$1 millin and A$1.5 million. Page B3.

Hire Intelligence, a computer rental franchise business, has transformed its cash-strapped Perth-based business operation into a national franchise network boasting a client list that includes government departments, BHP and WMC. Page B3.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373 1800
